title: Automatically refresh public outputs after published content changes
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned. As a publication editor, I want public outputs to refresh automatically whenever a saved change affects published content, so that readers and applications see consistent current publication state without a separate manual rebuild. Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet): ```gherkin Feature: Automatically refresh public outputs after published content changes Scenario: Save a change to publicly published content Given an item has a publicly published version and public delivery channels are configured When I save a change that updates its publicly published content Then its public article representation and affected listings and indexes are automatically updated And the sitemap and both RSS and Atom feeds reflect the same selected published version and metadata And headless outputs are updated when enabled And stable item identity, canonical links and publication versus update timestamps remain consistent Scenario: Publish or unpublish an item Given an item can enter or leave public publication under the existing authorized lifecycle When it is published or unpublished Then the article, affected listings and indexes, sitemap, RSS and Atom consistently reflect its public eligibility within the documented freshness bound And enabled headless outputs reflect the same eligibility And delayed older work cannot restore withdrawn or superseded public content Scenario: Save a private draft Given an item is unpublished or has a private draft newer than its public version When I save changes only to the private draft Then no draft text, draft metadata or draft-only asset appears in any public article, listing, index, sitemap, feed or headless output And an existing published version remains the public source until an authorized public change occurs Scenario: An ancillary public projection fails Given an authorized content change has been saved but an affected ancillary output fails to refresh When the editor or operator inspects the outcome Then saved-content success and each known failed or pending public update are distinguishable And the failed update is visible and has a supported retry or reconciliation path And retry converges affected public outputs to current authorized published state without duplicate feed identities or revived withdrawn content Scenario: Derive dependencies from a saved listing construct Given a page contains a supported declarative listing with item or issue type and featured selection parameters When the page is saved or compiled Then its affected-content registration is derived automatically from those same rendering parameters And the generated reverse index associates matching eligible content with the page And no separate manually duplicated per-page predicate configuration is required And publication visibility and authorization are enforced independently of selection Scenario: Refresh the union of old and new matches Given pages contain several supported listing components with different type and featured selections When a new eligible item is added or a published item is removed, unpublished or changes type or featured state Then affected pages are the union of pages matching either the old or new published state And every component's dependencies contribute to that union And bounded listings refresh when a candidate can enter or displace an entry And private drafts never become eligible merely because featured selection allows either value Scenario: Replace or remove stale page registrations Given a compiled listing page has generated dependency registrations When its listing selection is changed and the page is saved or recompiled Then the new registrations replace its stale registrations When the listing page is deleted Then its reverse-index registrations are removed Scenario: A custom dynamic query is not supported declaratively Given a custom embedded query has no supported declarative dependency representation When its page's dependency behavior is designed Then the unsupported capability and conservative fallback decision remain explicit And the plan does not claim automatic analysis of arbitrary application code ``` General Papyrus platform behavior, not a one-site sitemap audit. Both RSS and Atom are desired and share selection and metadata with the common foundation. Specify observable freshness, completion/failure reporting, retry/reconciliation and cache behavior before implementation. Orchestration, sequencing and atomicity remain design choices; do not prescribe a new service. Reuse/extend existing publish/save/unpublish and Markus/S3 incremental projection evidence (M3 PPY-3d905d) rather than invent a parallel publisher. Existing implementation evidence does not prove coverage of the new feed/headless outputs. RSS/Atom is the simplest first implementation candidate discussed; Monitoring may offer greater benefit, but neither implementation has been authorized. Approved dependency design (supersedes any manual per-page predicate-configuration proposal): convention over configuration. Derive dependencies automatically from supported declarative listing/embedded-content constructs when the containing page is saved or compiled. The listing's existing selection parameters are the sole source of truth for rendering and invalidation; never ask editors to maintain a parallel per-page predicate file or separately copied rule. Generate a reverse index associating matching content with affected pages from those constructs. Initial predicate scope is item/issue type plus featured true, false or either; publication scope, published eligibility and existing authorization are separate enforced gates, never optional query filters. Multiple listing components on one page contribute the union of dependencies. A public content change refreshes pages whose derived selection matches either old OR new published state, covering new items, removals, unpublish and type/featured transitions, including candidates that can enter or displace a bounded listing. Saving/recompiling an edited listing page replaces its old registrations; deleting it removes stale reverse-index entries. Keep original ordering, limit and other supported selection semantics from the rendering construct rather than restating them for invalidation. Design questions remain: exact Markus versus Papyrus extension ownership, declarative construct/schema syntax and supported selection vocabulary; mapping current tag-based custom listings onto the proposed item/issue-type and featured semantics; index persistence/rebuild, freshness and failure handling; and a conservative fallback for unsupported custom dynamic queries. Do not claim generic arbitrary-Python/React/code analysis. No listing markup syntax is approved or asserted to exist by this plan. Orchestration and atomicity remain design choices; no new service is prescribed. Verified read-only source evidence, AnthusAI/Anth.us-web main 5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7 (not the older default develop/local checkout): web/anthus_pages.py homepage at line404 constructs the Recent posts section from posts[:3] image cards and posts[3:10] dated links; the output contains `
    {thumbs}
` and an optional `
    {posts_items}
`. These are Python-generated HTML fragments, not an authored Markus listing directive/node/plugin or runtime React listing. web/anthus_content.py:448 Collections.from_nodes selects published, non-folded, non-platform blog nodes tagged posts, ordered by descending date with source-name ties; this is not proof of a general item-type/featured construct. web/build_via_papyrus.py:470 generate_pages calls pages.homepage with collections, _generated at408 stores the fragment, and write_generated at704 wraps it with markus_shell.render_page directly, bypassing Markus body conversion. web/projector.py:369 Snapshot.inputs hashes each generated page title plus rewritten fragment, the sitemap bytes and public-data bytes; listing_inputs at557 exposes those digests to the existing incremental mechanism. Thus existing fragment-digest invalidation is a reuse candidate, but no construct-derived reverse index or generic dependency extraction is established by that source. Explicitly bridge the current custom-generator gap during design rather than inventing existing syntax or promising to infer arbitrary code. Source links: - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/anthus_pages.py#L404 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/anthus_content.py#L448 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/build_via_papyrus.py#L470 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/build_via_papyrus.py#L704 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/projector.py#L369 This inspection establishes source behavior, not a fresh live-deployment audit. Existing M3 PPY-3d905d work is preserved; implementation remains unstarted for this extension.

comments.text: Revised dependency planning delivery on develop: validated all 39 planning records through Kanbus readback, including legal foundation/child hierarchy, exact descriptions, Gherkin and dependency targets. Full-board validation remains at the same 15 pre-existing dependency errors. Foundation and post-save behavior now specify construct-derived dependency extraction, one rendering-selection source, generated reverse index, component unions, old/new published-state matching and stale-entry removal. Feed/headless guides and delivery review updated. Pinned Anth.us main custom Python/fragment-digest evidence and design gaps recorded. No code, migration, deployment or new service; implementation remains unstarted.
